name: feature-flags
intro: The 10 feature flags of OpenCTI 7.261119.0: features still in development, hidden until the platform lists them in `app:enabled_dev_features` (see the [configuration reference](/reference/opencti/configuration/)). Reserved to development and not supported: a flagged feature can change or disappear in any release, so leave flags off in production; the guides describe the platform without them, and a feature is documented when a release removes its flag.
filter: Filter flags, API fields and screens

cells: Adds a **Use** access right between view and edit on restricted entities and organizations, and limits the author and authorized-member pickers to the identities the user can use.
Configuration presets, to export and import bundles of platform configuration, and the bootstrap wizard that offers one to the first administrator of a new platform.
The **Health** screen in **Data > Health**, listing the operations of the data sanity manager (the manager itself runs without the flag).
Connector versions decoupled from the platform version, with the connector catalog synchronized from XTM Hub (or a custom catalog endpoint) and update notices on deployed connectors.
A background check of the search engine every minute that logs its cluster health, node and thread pool statistics.
The extended workflow engine for every entity type (transitions, bypass, status cleanup); without it, only drafts use it and other types keep the classic status workflow.
Skip the import of entities unchanged since the last import by the same user
The ingestion health of connectors and feeds, computed by the ingestion health manager, with health alerts on deployed connectors in **Integrations** and a health email notifier.
Local authentication lockout policy feature flag
Logout a session once its last browser tab is closed, until its Phase 2 (shared presence) and Phase 3 (hardening)

sections.title: Turn a flag on
sections.text: A flag turns its feature on for the whole platform; no flag is set per user or per organization.

cells: The list of flags to turn on, in the platform configuration file. Read once when the platform starts: restart it after a change. The front reads the same list from the platform settings.
The same list as an environment variable, written as a JSON array.
Turns every flag on, in the back end and the front, including the flags of features not listed here.

sections.title: Flags the platform sets by itself
sections.text: The platform adds these to the flags the front reads; `app:enabled_dev_features` does not set them.

cells: Sorting lists on fields computed at query time, turned on by the platform when the search engine is Elasticsearch 7.12 or later. The `*` value of `app:enabled_dev_features` also turns it on in the front.
